propositions: Current review gate runners cannot distinguish clean execution from failed, cancelled, skipped, budget-shed, or resumed work outcomes, causing plan-review failures to become empty successful checkpoints and code review to lose earlier work when later criteria raise.

A new independent discovery submodule under rebar.llm.review_kernel must define immutable typed input plans and six distinct per-unit outcome types (success, resumed, skipped, shed, failed, cancelled) with deterministic dependency-aware scheduling and explicit budget shedding.

The executor must preserve successful independent results after exhausted local operations, mark dependents of missing work as skipped with dependency reason, and abort remaining work on systemic failures or cancellation with exact completed-so-far accounting.

A versioned, digest-complete envelope whose identity covers material, code, effective policy, prompt, contract, model, mode, topology, dependencies, and namespace version must round-trip only success and content-identical resumed units as reusable; failed, cancelled, skipped, and shed units remain missing.
Deterministic budget shedding by ascending (dependency rank, unit id) order produces an identical shed set across runs, with zero valid as disablement rejection and omission treated as uncapped.

Stored trace must contain normalized outcome metadata and lineage (ids, outcomes, reasons, usage) while excluding raw prompts, ticket/context bodies, provider responses, and secrets, with public review result schemas unchanged.
